DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 19 s. 2022 7 April 2022 PUNONG BARANGAY EDUARD PANGAN Municipality of Paniqui Province of Tarlac Dear PB Pangan: This refers to your letter dated January 21 , 2022 requesting for this Departments legal opinion on the following issues, which we herein quoted in toto: "I. 2. 3. Whether the absence of Approved Municipal Resolution/Ordinance on Rules on Administrative Investigation by the Sangguniang Bayan of Paniqui, Tarlac invalidates or nullify the Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 01 II-s2021 for violation of due process guaranteed by 1987 Constitution; Whether the six (6) months suspension being imposed by the Municipal Mayor Hon. Leonardo M. Roxas be automatically lifted after December 31, 2021; and Whether an OIC of Barangay can terminate the services of Barangay Treasurer and Barangay Secretary." As represented in your letter, hereunder are the pertinent factual antecedents, to wit: 1. On May I, 2021, you assumed the Office of the Punong Barangay (PB) pursuant to rule on succession due to the sudden death of the incumbent PB; 2. On December 7, 2021 you received an Executive Order of Suspension for six (6) months from the Office of the Municipal Mayor Hon. Leonardo M. Roxas. The aforesaid suspension order emanated from the recommendation of the Sangguniang Bayan of Paniqui, Tarlac under Resolution No. 0111-s2021 ; 3. The Barangay Secretary issued five (5) Barangay Clearances without Official Receipts (OR) for their payments due to unavailability of OR but the Secretary wrote down the names of the five (5) residents on the record book. The former Barangay Treasurer failed to properly tum over the Official Receipts to the new Barangay Treasurer. However, the total amount of One Hundred Fifty Pesos (P 150.00) being collected from the complainants were properly recorded in the Barangay Logbook and the amount was deposited to the bank account of Barangay Manaois accordingly; 4. The complainants did not state the administrative grounds under the Local Govemment Code of charge filed against you. Neither was is stated in the summons sent by the Committee Chair on Barangay Affairs; Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

5. Before the Committee Hearing, you submitted a Motion of Bill of Particulars. The same duly received by the Sangguniang Secretary but until today, the same has not been resolved; 6. A committee hearing was held on October 26, 2021 but the procedure was summary in nature. You were not given a chance to cross-examine the complainants. You were only informed verbally during the committee hearing and was not given a chance to properly answer the administrative grounds and defend yourself in accordance with law; 7. After you received the Suspension Order, you sent a letter to the Sangguniang Secretary requesting for a copy of the Rules on Administrative Investigation by the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Paniqui, Tarlac and found out that the SB has no approved ordinances of Rules on Administrative Investigation by the SB of Paniqui, Tarlac; 8. On December 15, 2021 you submitted a Motion for Reconsideration. However, presently there was no session to review your motion for reconsideration. You also requested that a hearing be scheduled on December 20, 2021 at 1 :OOPM, but the SB did not conduct a hearing; 9. You are of the belief that your immediate suspension of six (6) month was too excessive, cruel and harsh. You reason that the allegations against you were too general and the complaints has no factual and legal bases. The inaction of the SB on the Motions that you submitted prevented you from filing the necessary appeal from the Office of the Sanggniang Panlalawigan because the case is still pending before the SB; 10. You wrote a letterfor resumption of office and it was received by OIC Januario M. Pasion, Jr and members of the Sangguniang Barangay of Manaois declaring that you are resuming office and that your suspension has been automatically lifted pursuant to Section 63 of the Local Government Code; 11. On the same date, You also submitted letter to the Office of the Municipal Mayor and to the Office of the SB informing them that you shall be deemed reinstated in the office pursuant to the Local Govemment Code; 12. Upon submission of the letters to the concemed parties, you immediately reported to Barangay Hall. You and the Barangay Treasurer went to Land Bank of Paniqui Branch to settle salary loans and honoraria but the transaction was denied; 13. Since you resumed Office you have been signing all the Brgy. Clearances/ Certificates being requested by the residents. However, the Municipal Mayor's Office refused to accept and recognize your signature— all municipal departments and employees of the Municipal Hall were advised to not recognize you as Punong Barangay. Hence, the issued Brgy. Certificates were retumed, and subsequently, request for refund were made. Under such premise, arose your request for this Departments opinion on the above- stated issues. Page 2 of 9

Thereafter, you followed-up your request. For this, we asked you if you could give us a copy of the Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 0111 -s. 2021 , which you readily gave us. Pertinent portion of said Sangguniang Bayan Resolution reads: "WHEREAS, on October 12, 2021 Regular Session, a resolution was adopted (Resolution No. 086-s2021) constituting the Sangguniang Bayan into a Committee of the Whole to conduct inquiry land investigation on the Administrative Complaint (Administrative Case No. 02-2021) to be chaired by the chairman of the Committee on Barangay Affairs; WHEREAS, the SB Secretary was directed to notify all parties concemed to appear on the scheduled Committee Hearings of the Committee of the Whole on October 19, 2021 and October 26, 2021; WHEREAS, after the issues have been formally joined and a thorough review and examination of the documental and testimonial evidence presented by both parties concemed in the instant administrative case was properly taken and due process have been observed and complied with, pursuant to Article III of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, the committee strongly believe that there is a probable cause supported by substantial evidence submitted for consideration during the hearing as well as those contained in the records and made known to the parties affected. WHEREAS, the following are the findings of the committee, to wit: I. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. There should be no collection of money/payment without an approved tax ordinance of the Barangay. There should be no collection of any amount of money concem in the barangay without issuing an offcial receipt. There was not resolution made by the Punong Barangay and Sangguniang Barangay members allowing the Barangay Secretary to collect and sign on his behalf on all documents issued by the Barangay. Upon resumption from offce, the Punong Barangay shall have reviewed all the By-Laws, Tax Ordinances and all concemed documents and remind all concemed officials especially the Barangay Treasurer and the Barangay Secretary to refer on all Tax Ordinances. The Punong Barangay only issued a Memorandum dated October 18, 2021 , reminding the Barangay Secretary and Barangay Treasurer regarding the issuance of official receipt, this action of the Punong Barangay was made only after they have received a complaint for non-compliance of the Barangay Tax Ordinance for collecting payment without issuing an official receipt. Based on the counter affdavit submitted, it showed the delinquency of the barangay officials concemed for not including the collection of payment of the Barangay Clearance on the report of collections and deposits for the reason that they are still on the transition period. This action only proved that they did not deposit the said collection, for they only deposited the payments from the issuance of Barangay Certification upon receiving of the complaint against them. WHEREAS, this action made by the Punong Barangay and Barangay Secretary proved of their wrongdoing for violation of Sec 60 paragraph (c) and (e) of RA 7160, identified as misconduct of offce, dereliction of duty and abuse of authority; Page 3 of 9

NOW THEREFORE, on motion of Councilor Linda B. Manuel (ABC), duly seconded by Councilor Robert J. Torio, that respondent Punong Barangay Eduard Y. Pangan be placed under immediate SUSPENSION for a period of Six (6) months; The Order dated December 2, 2021 issued by Mayor Leonardo M. Roxas to implement said Order reads: "Bilang pagtalima sa isinasaad ng desisyon ng Sangguniang Bayan ng Paniqui na may pamagat na Resolution Bilang 0111-s2021, ikaw ay pinapatawan ng anim (6) na buwan na suspension epektibo mula sa araw ng pagkakatanggap ng order na ito. Kalakip ng order na ito ang Resolution Bilang 0111-s2021 para sa iyong kaalaman. Upon evaluation of the documents forwarded to the Department, it appears that you are of the belief that the 6-month suspension subject of Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 0111-s. 2021 and imposed by Mayor Roxas through an Order dated December 2, 2021 is preventive suspension as you consistently mentioned the term "automatic lifting" and Section 631 of RA 7160 or the Local Govemment Code of 1991 which both pertain to preventive suspension. This can also be deduced from your number 2 query, that is, "(VV)hether the six (6) months suspension being imposed by the Municipal Mayor Hon. Leonardo M. Roxas be automatically lifted after December 31. 2021?" This is also apparent in your letters all dated January 10, 2022 to Acting Punong Barangay Januario M. Pasion, Sangguniang Barangay Members, Municipal Mayor Roxas, and Sangguniang Bayan Members. However, we are not convinced that the suspension imposed was preventive suspension as the period involved was 6 months, hence, way too long for a preventive suspension. Under Section 63 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991, preventive suspension can be 60 days only. 1 SECTION 63. Prevenüve Suspenion. (a) Preventive suspension rnay be imposed: (1) By the President, if the respondent is an Offdal of a province, a highly urbanized or an independent component city; (2) By the governor, if the respondent is an ofidal Of a convorEnt dty or munidpality; (3) By the mayor. if the respmdent is an elective offdal Of (b) Preventive suspension may be imposed at any time aner the issues are Mwn evidence of guilt is strong. and given the gravity of the there is great probability that the continuanæ in offce of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of ttE records and other evidence: Provided, That. any single preventive suspension of local eledive offcials shall not extend beyond sixty (60) days: Provided. furtier, That in the event that several administrative cases are fibd an eledive offcial, he cannot be preventively suspended for more than ninety (90) days within a year on the same ground or grounds existing and known at time of the first suspension. (c) Upon expiration of the preventive suspa•lsion, the suspended elective offcial shall be deemed reinstated in without prejudice to the continuation of the proceedings against him. whidl shall be terminated within one hundred tænty (120) days frorn the time he was forrnaliy notified of the case against him. However, if the delay in the of the case is due to his neglect. or request. other than the appeal duly filed, tle duration of such delay shall not be counted in computing tie time of termination of the case. (d) Any abuse of the exercise of the of preventive suspension shall be penalized as abuse of Page 4 of 9

At this juncture, it may be well to differentiate preventive suspension from suspension as a penalty. Preventive suspension imposed by the sanggunian/Ofice of the President upon an erring local elective official is govemed by Section 63 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 while suspension as a penalty is already govemed by Section 66 of the same Code. Section 62 (c) of the Local Govemment Code also provides that at the onset of the 90-day period prior to local election, the preventive suspension earlier imposed shall be deemed automatically lifted. This "automatic lifting" is not applicable in the case of suspension as a penalty. Jurisprudence is replete with cases establishing a clear cut distinction between suspension as a preventive measure and suspension as a penalty. In Quimbo vs. Gervaci02, the Supreme Court differentiated these two (2) terms/concepts in the following manner: "Preventive suspension is merely a preventive measure, a preliminary step in the administrative investigation. The purpose of the suspension order is to prevent the accused from using his position and the powers and prerogatives of his office to influence potential witnesses or tamper with records which may be vital in the prosecution of the case against him. If after such investigation, the charge is established and the person investigated is found guilty of acts warranting his suspension or removal, then he is suspended, removed or dismissed. This is the penalty." In Section 66 of the Local Govemment Code, the Sanggunian concemed (disciplining authority) is mandated to render a decision in writing stating therein clearly and distinctly the facB and the reasons for such decision. It seems that the Sangguniang Bayan of Paniqui, when it adopted Resolution No. 0111-s2021 , has not clearly written the decision with the end view that you are apprised of the contents thereof as well as the ruling upon you. This is important so that you, as respondent, could avail the proper remedies under the law. Upon reading Resolution No. 0111-s2021, the 5th Whereas Clause of Resolution No. 0111-2.2021 mentioned that there was a formal joinder of the issues and then in the 6th Whereas Clause state the findings of the Committee only. This might have prompted you to think that you are under preventive suspension since preventive suspension is imposed after the issues are joined. The Decision also did not mention the filing of an Answer by the Respondent when in the documents you recently submitted during your follow-up, you submitted an Answer on October 7, 2021. However, going back to your first query on whether the absence of Approved Municipal Resolution/Ordinance on Rules on Administrative Investigation by the Sangguniang Bayan of Paniqui, Tarlac invalidates or nullifies the Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 0111-s2021 for violation of due process guaranteed by 1987 Constitution, we reply in the negative. The absence of such Rules will not motu proprio invalidate the Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 0111-s2021 since such Rules merely govem the conduct of the members themselves and ensure the orderly discharge of their functions, hence, procedural. 2 G.R. No. 155620.09 August 2005. Page 5 of 9

In Vivo vs, PAGC(W, the Supreme Court explained what constitutes due process in administrative cases: "The observance of faimess in the conduct of any investigation is at the very heart of procedural due process. The essence of due process is to be heard, and, as applied to administrative proceedings, this means a fair and reasonable opportunity to explain one's side, or an opportunity to seek a reconsideration of the action or ruling complained of. Administrative due process cannot be fully equated with due process in its strict judicial sense, for in the former a formal or trial-type hearing is not always necessary, and technical rules of procedure are not strictly applied. Ledesma v. Court of Appeals elaborates on the well-established meaning of due process in administrative proceedings in this wise: x x x Due process, as a constitutional precept, does not always and in all situations require a trial-type proceeding. Due process is satisfied when a person is notified of the charge against him and given an opportunity to explain or defend himself. In administrative proceedings. the filing of charges and qivinq reasonable opportunity for the person so charged to answer the accusations against him constitute the minimum requirements of due process. The essence of due process is simply to be heard, or as applied to administrative proceedings, an opportunity to explain one's side, or an opportunity to seek a reconsideration of the action or ruling complained of." (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the documents you recently forwarded to the Departrnent, it appears that: 1. A letter dated September 22, 2021 was issued by Hon. Linda Manuel, Chairperson, Committee on Barangay Affairs, informing you that a Verified Administrative Complaint was filed against you; 2. In the same letter, Hon. Manuel required you to file your Verified Answer within 15 days from receipt thereof; 3. A letter dated October 13, 2021 was issued by Hon. Manuel requesting you to attend the committee hearing on October 19, 2021 regarding the latter's administrative case; 4. Another letter dated October 21, 2021 was issued by Hon. Manuel requesting you to another Committee hearing on October 26, 2021 ; 5. You submitted an Answer dated October 7, 2021; and 6. In the 4th Whereas Clause of Resolution No. 01 II-s2021, it was stated that the SB Secretary was directed to notify all parties concemed to appear on the scheduled Committee hearings of the Committee of the Whole on October 19, 2021 and October 26, 2021. We are of the view that the foregoing complied the requirement on due process. If such Rules that you are referring as lacking is the Intemal Rules of Procedure required under Section 50 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991to be adopted or updated by the concemed Sanggunian, while the same does not also invalidates Resolution No. 0111-s2021, it may be a ground against the Sanggunian Bayan Members of Paniqui for possible dereliction or neglect of duty for failure to comply with 3 G.R No. 187854, 12 November 2013. Page 6 of 9

the requirements of law. Note that under Section 50 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 , IRP may adopt such other rules as the Sanggunian may adopt. As to the second query, as mentioned, the term "automatic lifting" is used only when referring to preventive suspension and not in the case of suspension as a penalty. In the letters dated January IO, 2022 addressed to the Acting Punong Barangay Januario M. Pasion, Sangguniang Barangay Members, Municipal Mayor Roxas, and Sangguniang Bayan Members, the reason you invoked to justify your automatic reinstatement to office is that the year 2021 has already ended so that he is deemed reinstated in office beginning January I , 2022. Such ground you invoked has no basis in law. Besides, what is critical is the fact of valid service of the decision for the respondent to properly reckon the commencement of serving his penalty. On the other hand, we have Section 62 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 which contemplates a situation of the automatic lifting of the preventive suspension at the onset of the 90-day period prior to local election, that is, starting on February 8, 2022. "SECTION 62. Notice of Hearing. xxxx (c) However, no investigation shall be held within ninety (90) days immediately prior to any local election, and no preventive suspension shall be imposed within the said period. If preventive suspension has been imposed prior to the 90-day period immediately preceding local election. it shall be deemed lifted upon the start of aforesaid period " Since, as we have stated, the suspension imposed upon you appears to be suspension as a penalty, you may not invoke this provision of law. On the last query, attention is respectfully directed to Section 46 of the Code, thus: "Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) When the govemor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concemed, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period Of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. (b) Said temporary incapacity shall terminate upon submission to the appropriate sanggunian of a written declaration by the local chief executive concemed that he has reported back to office. In cases where the temporary incapacity is due to legal causes, the local chief executive concemed shall also submit necessary documents showing that said legal causes no longer exist. Xxx." As can be clearly gathered from the afore-quoted provision, the Acting Punong Barangay may exercise the power to dismiss employees, including Barangay Page 7 of 9

Treasure and Barangay Secretary, if the period of temporary incapacity in the office of the incumbent Punong Barangay exceeds thirty (30) working days. However, there is an important caveat here, such act has to be anchored on a just cause. The Acting PB cannot just remove employees and subsequently replace them sans valid and just cause. Insofar as the appointment or replacement of appointive barangay officials is concemed, Section 389 of the Code provides: "Section 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. — (b) For efficient, effective and economical govemance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the punong barangay shall: (5) Upon approval by a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay, appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials. Xxx." (Emphasis supplied) The Supreme Court, in the case of Alquizola et. v. Ocol et. al.4, had explained the above-cited provision of the Code, thus: "The term "replace" would obviously embrace not only the appointment of the replacement but also the prior removal of, or the vacation by, the official currently occupying the appointive position concemed. " To replace" is to take the place of, to serve as a substitute for or successor of, to put in place of, or to fill the post of an incumbent. In order to provide a replacement to an office, the prior holder must have first been removed or the offce must have, otherwise, been previously rendered vacant. Aside from what may be implicit in Section 389, there is no other provision in the Local Govemment Code that treats of the power of the Punong Barangay to remove the barangay secretary, the barangay treasurer, or any other appointive barangay official from office. The duration of the term of office of these barangay officials have not been fixed by the Local Govemment Code. Where the tenure of the office is not fixed by law, it is a sound and useful rule to consider the power of removal as being an incident to the power of appointment. Elsewise stated, the power to remove is deemed implied in the power to appoint. The Code explicitly vests on the punong barangay, upon approval by a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay, the power to appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials. This provision is reinforced, in the case of the secretary and the treasurer, by the provisions of Section 394 and Section 395 of the Local Govemment Code; to wit: Sec. 394. Barangay Secretary: Appointment, Qualifications, Powers and Duties. — (a) The barangay secretary shall be appointed by the punong barangay with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang 4 G.R. No. 132413, dated 27 August 1999. Page 8 of 9

barangay members. The appointment of the barangay secretary shall not be subject to attestation by the Civil Service Commission. Sec. 395. Barangay Treasurer. Appointment, Qualifications, Powers and Duties. — (a) The barangay treasurer shall be appointed by the punong barangay with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang barangay members. The appointment of the barangay treasurer shall not be subject to attestation by the Civil Service Commission. Verily, the power of appointment is to be exercised conjointly by the punong barangay and a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay. Without such conjoint action, neither an appointrnent nor a replacement can be effectual. Applying the rule that the power to appoint includes the power to remove, one that the Court finds no cogent reason to now depart from, the questioned dismissal from office of the barangay officials by the punong barangay without the concurrence of the majority of all the members of the Sangguniang Barangay cannot be legally justified. To rule otherwise could also create an absurd situation of the Sangguniang Barangay members refusing, like here, to give their approval to the replacements selected by the punong barangay who has unilaterally terminated the services of the incumbents. It is likely that the legislature did not intend this absurdity to flow from its enactment of the law." The foregoing pronouncement of the Supreme Court is instructive. It bears to stress that while punong barangays, or in the herein case acting punong barangay pursuant to Section 46 of the Code, can remove any of the appointed barangay appointive officials, including the barangay treasurer and the barangay secretary, the same should be approved by the majority of all members of the Sanggniang barangay. Please note that the foregoing opinion is based solely on the facts contained in your letter-request and our appreciation of the same. Lastly, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
